name: Shiftwise
oneLiner: Shift scheduling and labour forecasting software for warehouses and distribution centres.
whatItDoes: Forecasts labour demand per shift from order volumes, inbound shipments and historical pick rates.
Builds shift rosters automatically, respecting skills, contracts, overtime rules and time-off requests.
Lets workers swap shifts and pick up open shifts from a phone app, with manager approval rules.
Shows supervisors a live view of planned versus actual labour hours per zone.

pricing.model: Per active worker per month, billed annually.
pricing.listPrice: $9 per worker per month. A 400-worker site is about $43,200 a year.
pricing.implementation: One-off onboarding fee of $12,000 per site, covering integration and training.
pricing.discountRules: Up to 10% off list for a 3-year commitment. Up to 15% for 3+ sites signed together. No other discounts are authorised.

proof: 42 customer sites live, all in logistics and light manufacturing.
Typical (median) result: overtime hours down 9% in the first six months.
Best result: one 3PL customer, Harbourline Logistics (fictional), cut overtime 18% and agency spend 22% in a year.
Average onboarding time: 7 weeks per site.
limitations: No native payroll; integrates with three payroll systems only (the rest need a CSV export).
The forecasting model needs at least 6 months of order history to be accurate.
The company is 4 years old with 60 employees; some buyers see that as a risk.

competitors.name: Kronara
competitors.position: Large incumbent workforce suite. Broad, expensive, slow to change.

competitors.name: RotaPilot
competitors.position: Cheap self-serve scheduling app. Fine for small sites, weak forecasting.

competitors.name: Spreadsheets and supervisor judgement
competitors.position: The real status quo at most sites.
